prompt:
Warm editorial ink-and-wash illustration on a warm cream ground: a loose confident ink line with soft transparent washes over it, muted earth palette of cream, rust, ochre, mustard, sage and warm grey, quiet and hand-made, the register of a good picture book rather than a comic. Object reference: PIP, a small hand-made helper machine. It is A SMALL DENTED TIN-AND-WOOD BOX roughly THE SIZE OF A LOAF OF BREAD, standing on THREE THIN SPLAYED BRASS LEGS. On its front face there is ONE ROUND GLASS LENS set in a brass ring, and beside the lens ONE SMALL BRASS HORN that it speaks through. ONE JOINTED BRASS ARM is folded against its side, ending in a plain two-finger pincer. There is ONE VERY SMALL AMBER PILOT BULB, dim and warm, which does NOT glow and does NOT cast light on anything. The tin is dented, scratched and patinated, obviously made by hand. Shown from a front three-quarter angle, sitting on a plain empty cream background. CRITICAL: IT HAS NO FACE. No eyes, no eyebrows, no mouth, no expression. The lens is a LENS, like a camera lens or a light meter, and must NOT read as an eye. It is NOT a cute robot, NOT humanoid, has NO head, NO torso, NO pair of arms, NO legs other than the three thin brass tripod legs. No glowing screens, no holograms, no blue light, no display, no dials with faces. Render ONE single image only. This is NOT a contact sheet, NOT a grid, NOT a multi-panel study sheet, NOT a turnaround strip. No panel borders, no captions, no labels, no annotation text of any kind. ABSOLUTELY NOT, these are the rejected poles of this style and any of them is a failure: neon, 3D or CGI or Pixar rendering, glossy plastic, HUD or arc-reactor comic vocabulary, neo-comic styling, photorealism, airbrushing, lens flare, heavy drop shadows.

DEVICE ANATOMY, NON-NEGOTIABLE: any phone, laptop, tablet or monitor is anatomically correct. The GLOWING DISPLAY is on the SCREEN side, and that side FACES ITS USER. A person looking at a device sees its screen; the viewer therefore sees the device's BACK or EDGE plus the light it throws onto the user's face and hands. NEVER put the screen image on the back of a phone, on a laptop's outer lid, or on a monitor's rear. NEVER show a screen facing the camera while the person using it looks at the opposite side. If both the user's face and the screen content must be visible, shoot it over the user's shoulder.

READABLE SURFACES FACE THEIR READER: any book, page, letter, scroll or sign a character is reading or writing faces THAT CHARACTER, never the camera. Compose over-the-shoulder or from behind so the surface genuinely faces them. Any handwriting is abstract handwriting-like line work with NO real readable letters.

NO USER INTERFACE ANYWHERE: no windows, menu bars, buttons, icons, toolbars, panels, form fields, cursors, floating rectangles or screenshot-like elements. Screens carry only soft glow or vague painterly shapes.
